walkthrough: Goal: take back a stroke that went wrong, and bring it back if that was a mistake.

Entry: the app is open on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape). The side bar at the left edge holds, under its two sliders, two arrows: undo (turning back left) above redo (turning back right). Both are dim grey: nothing has been drawn yet.
Draw a curve with the pen, then a second stroke below it. Undo turns light: it can be tapped. Redo stays grey.
Tap undo with a finger: the second stroke disappears at once and redo turns light. Tap undo again: the canvas is blank and undo greys out. Tapping the grey undo does nothing.
Tap redo with the pen tip: the first stroke returns; tapping a button with the pen leaves no ink. Tap redo again: both strokes are back and redo greys out.
Undo once and draw a third stroke instead: the undone stroke is gone for good, so redo is grey again.

While the pen is on the canvas both arrows keep their look (since S14), but history waits until the stroke is lifted: a tap then is refused, so the stroke in progress is never lost or drawn onto a version that is no longer shown.
Not here: two-finger tap to undo (s14-view-gestures), history surviving a restart.
